newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Aalberts aims for continued EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: Aalberts aims for continued EPS growth.

text.p: Dutch industrial holding company Aalberts Industries said on Thursday it would aim for continued earnings per share growth in the coming years.

"For the last ten years, we've had an annual increase of some 20 percent. I'm not going to give you a detailed forecast, but we do intend to ensure continuity in the development of earnings per share," company president Jan Aalberts said.
Aalberts said he expected growth in 1997 to be similar to that in 1996.
Aalberts also said that stock levels had risen sharply to 169 million guilders last year, mainly due to two acquisitions, from 102 million the previous year.
"Something has to be done about that. We'll consider the (level of) stocks in case of other acquisitions," he said.
Aalberts, which makes and sells installation materials, dispensing systems and special components, had 1996 net profit of 26.2 million guilders, up 30 percent on 1995.
Turnover last year was 471 million guilders, up 29 percent.
